MARS 360 – NASA Space Apps Challenge Project Summary
MARS 360 is an interactive Mars exploration and survival planning application designed to help future astronauts plan safer Marswalk missions. It combines NASA datasets from MOLA, CTX, THEMIS, and HiRISE into one interactive Mars map.
The application will include four main features:
Mars Explorer: Explore Mars using scientific map layers and select locations.
Terrain Analyzer: Examine elevation, slopes, surface features, and potential hazards.
Route Planner: Create Marswalk routes, calculate distances, and compare alternative paths.
Survival Simulator: Estimate astronauts' oxygen, water, and battery consumption during missions.
details:
MARS 360 – Explore Mars. Plan Your Route. Survive the Mission.

1. Project Overview

MARS 360 is an interactive Mars exploration and astronaut survival planning application that combines NASA scientific datasets into a unified planetary map. It helps users explore Martian terrain, identify potential hazards, plan astronaut routes, and simulate resource consumption during exploration missions.

2. Problem Statement

Planning human missions to Mars is challenging because scientific information about the planet is collected by different spacecraft and instruments. Understanding terrain, elevation, temperature, and environmental conditions is essential for planning exploration routes and future astronaut habitats.

3. Proposed Solution

MARS 360 integrates multiple NASA datasets into one interactive platform. Users can explore Mars, analyze surface conditions, create exploration routes, and evaluate whether astronauts have sufficient resources to complete their missions.

4. Main Features

1. Interactive Mars Explorer

  • Explore the Martian surface.
  • Zoom and select geographical locations.
  • Display different scientific map layers.

2. Terrain and Hazard Analyzer

  • Examine surface elevation and slopes.
  • Visualize terrain characteristics.
  • Identify areas requiring further investigation.

3. Marswalk Route Planner

  • Select starting and destination locations.
  • Create routes with intermediate points.
  • Calculate approximate travel distances.
  • Compare alternative routes.

4. Astronaut Survival Simulator

  • Calculate estimated oxygen consumption.
  • Monitor water and battery resources.
  • Simulate missions lasting 1, 7, or 30 days.
  • Generate resource warnings.

5. Mission Report

  • Display route information.
  • Summarize environmental evidence.
  • Show resource consumption and remaining supplies.

5. NASA Data Sources

  • MOLA – Mars elevation and topography.
  • CTX – Mars surface imagery.
  • THEMIS – Thermal infrared observations.
  • HiRISE – High-resolution surface imagery.

6. Technology Stack

  • Google Antigravity – AI-assisted development.
  • React – Frontend application.
  • Tailwind CSS – User interface design.
  • OpenLayers – Interactive planetary mapping.
  • JavaScript – Route and survival calculations.
  • Recharts – Data visualization.
  • Netlify – Application deployment.

7. Target Users

  • Future Mars astronauts.
  • Space researchers.
  • Planetary scientists.
  • Space exploration enthusiasts.
  • Students and educators.

8. Expected Impact

MARS 360 aims to make planetary scientific information easier to explore and understand by bringing multiple datasets together. It demonstrates how NASA open data can support informed Mars exploration planning and educational simulations.

9. Innovation

The main innovation is combining scientific Mars mapping, route planning, terrain analysis, and astronaut resource simulation into one interactive application.

10. Development Plan

The application will be developed using Google Antigravity AI. Our team will research NASA datasets, build the interface, integrate map services, implement route and survival calculations, test the application, and deploy the final prototype.

11. Project Goal

Our goal is to create a functional, interactive, and scientifically grounded Mars exploration platform that demonstrates how NASA data can help people understand and plan future human exploration of Mars.
